transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. My name is Alex. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hi Alex. I'm having a really frustrating issue with my mobile service. I keep dropping calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm very sorry to hear that. I can definitely look into what's going on with your service. To get started, could I please have your name and the phone number you're calling about?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sure. My name is Charles Williams, and the number is 555-156-9982.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Williams. For security purposes, to access your account, I need to verify a couple more details. Can you please provide me with your Customer ID?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, hold on, let me find it... Okay, it's CUST-1010.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, CUST-1010. And the last thing I need is the 4-digit security PIN you set up on the account.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It should be 1098.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent, thank you for verifying that information. I have your account pulled up now. So, you mentioned you're experiencing dropped calls. Can you tell me a little more about that? For instance, where does this typically happen?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's almost always when I'm at home. Specifically, when I'm in my basement. I have my home office down there, and it's becoming a real problem for my work calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly understand how frustrating that must be, especially when it's affecting your work. Is it only in the basement, or does it happen in other parts of your house as well?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's worst in the basement. Upstairs it's... okay. I might have one bar, maybe two. But downstairs, it's a total dead zone. The call connects, and then a minute later, it just drops.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's very helpful information. And what type of phone are you using, Mr. Williams?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's an iPhone. A 14, I think.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An iPhone 14. Got it. Thank you. Do you mind if I place you on a brief hold for about 60 to 90 seconds? I want to check our network coverage maps for your address and see if there are any known issues or physical obstructions.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, that's fine. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll be right back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Mr. Williams.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No problem. Find anything?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. So, I've reviewed the topography and our cell tower placement around your address. The outdoor signal strength in your neighborhood is rated as 'Good to Excellent'. There are no reported outages or tower maintenance activities.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So why can't I make a call from my basement?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the key question. What you're likely experiencing is something called signal attenuation. Cellular signals have a tough time penetrating dense materials. Things like concrete foundations, insulation, and earth itself can significantly weaken or block the signal from reaching your phone.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So my basement is basically a bunker for cell signals. That makes sense, I guess. So am I just out of luck?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all! In fact, I see something on your account that gives us a perfect solution. I see you also have our Cymbal Fiber Gigabit internet service at the same address.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I do, yes. The internet service is fantastic, no complaints there.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's great to hear. Because you have a strong, stable Wi-Fi connection from Cymbal in your home, we can use that to solve your calling problem. Have you ever heard of Wi-Fi Calling?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Wi-Fi Calling? I think I've seen the setting, but I don't really know what it is. Is it like using WhatsApp or FaceTime Audio?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a great question, and it's a common point of confusion. It's similar in that it uses the internet, but it's much more seamless. Wi-Fi Calling allows your phone to make and receive calls and text messages over your Wi-Fi network, but it still uses your regular phone number. People calling you won't know the difference.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So if I'm in my basement with no cell signal, but my Wi-Fi is working, my phone will ring and I can make calls normally?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. Your phone will intelligently switch over to your Cymbal Wi-Fi network for calls whenever the cellular signal is weak or unavailable. It's a free feature included with your plan.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Wow. Okay. That sounds... like exactly what I need. How do I turn it on?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can walk you through it right now. It's a simple process. Do you have your iPhone with you?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I'm holding it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. First, I just need to enable the feature on your line from my end. It's a quick change. Just one moment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, I've just provisioned Wi-Fi Calling for your number. Now we just need to enable it on your handset.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, ready.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Please go to your phone's home screen and tap on the 'Settings' app. It's the one that looks like a grey gear.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I'm in Settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Now, near the top, you should see an option for 'Cellular'. Please tap that.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yep, tapped it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the next menu, look for a section called 'Wi-Fi Calling'. Do you see it?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I see it. It says 'Off'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Please tap on 'Wi-Fi Calling'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now you should see a toggle switch that says 'Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone'. Please tap that switch to turn it on.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Done. A pop-up just appeared. It says 'Enable Wi-Fi Calling?' and has a lot of text about location and emergency calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's the final confirmation step. Go ahead and tap the 'Enable' button.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, enabled. Now it's loading a screen that says 'Emergency Address'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: This is a very important step, Mr. Williams. When you make a 911 call over a traditional cellular network, your location can be triangulated. With Wi-Fi, it can't. So you must provide the physical address where you'll be using Wi-Fi Calling most often.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Ah, so if I call 911 from my basement, they know where to send help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Precisely. It will likely have your billing address pre-filled. Can you confirm that the address shown is the correct physical address for your home?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, that's the right street address, city, state, and zip code.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. Please go ahead and tap the 'Save' or 'Confirm' button on that screen.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I've confirmed it. It took me back to the previous screen, and the toggle is now green and 'On'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic. That's it. You've successfully enabled Wi-Fi Calling on your phone.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That was easier than I thought. So how do I know if it's working?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great question. Look at the very top left of your phone's screen, in the status bar. Instead of just seeing 'Cymbal', you should now see 'Cymbal Wi-Fi' or 'Cymbal WiFi Calling'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Let me see... Yes! It says 'Cymbal Wi-Fi'. Wow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That means you're all set. Your phone is now prioritizing your Wi-Fi network for calls. Let's run a quick test to be absolutely sure it will work when you have no cell signal.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, how do we do that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We're going to simulate being in your basement with no cell service. Are you comfortable with navigating your phone's Control Center?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I use it all the time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Please swipe down from the top-right corner of your screen to open the Control Center.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, it's open.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now, please tap the airplane icon to turn on Airplane Mode. This will disconnect you from the cellular network. Don't worry, we are on a landline call right? Or are you on the mobile?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh, right. I'm calling you from my mobile. This call will drop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Ah, okay, good catch. My apologies. Let's adjust the plan. No need to turn on Airplane Mode right now. The fact that you see 'Cymbal Wi-Fi' in your status bar is a very strong indicator it's working.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So you're confident this will fix the dropped calls in the basement?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am very confident. As long as you have a stable Wi-Fi signal in your basement office, which you should with your Cymbal Fiber service, your phone will now use it for calls.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: My Wi-Fi router is upstairs. The signal is pretty good in the basement, but not full strength.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's generally okay. Wi-Fi calling doesn't require a huge amount of bandwidth, just a stable connection. If you find you still have issues, you might consider a Wi-Fi mesh system or an extender to ensure a stronger signal in the basement, but I would suggest trying it out as-is first.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, that's fair. I'll test it out on my next few calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Here's what I'd recommend. After we hang up, go down to your basement office. Put your phone in Airplane Mode, then manually turn Wi-Fi back on. You'll see the 'Cymbal Wi-Fi' status. Then try making a test call to a friend or even your own voicemail.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's a good idea. That will prove it works without any cell signal at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. It's the definitive test. You'll be making a call purely over your Cymbal Wi-Fi.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is great. I was honestly expecting you to tell me there was nothing you could do.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm so glad we could find a solution for you. Leveraging the services you already have with us is the best way to ensure you get the most value and performance. I'll add some detailed notes to your account, so if you ever call back, the next agent will know we've enabled this for you.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Thank you, I appreciate that. This could be a real game-changer for working from home.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome. It's designed for exactly this kind of situation. Is there anything else I can assist you with today, Mr. Williams? Perhaps a question about your internet service or billing?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, I think that's it. You've solved my main headache for the week. I'm very happy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's what I love to hear. Well, thank you for being a Cymbal Telecom customer. We appreciate your business. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too, Alex. Thanks again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Bye.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh! Alex, are you still there?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Mr. Williams, I'm still here. Is everything alright?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sorry, one last quick question just popped into my head. Does this cost extra? Like, does it use my plan's data or minutes?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An excellent and important question. I'm glad you asked. No, there is no extra charge for using Wi-Fi Calling for domestic calls within the United States. They are treated just like regular calls and billed against your plan's minutes, which I can see you have unlimited anyway.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, so no extra cost. What about data? Does it use my home internet data?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Technically yes, it uses a very small amount of data from your home internet connection. However, a voice call uses a tiny fraction of what streaming a video does. Since you have our Fiber Gigabit plan with unlimited data, you will never notice the usage or see any charges for it. It's effectively free.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, that's what I needed to know. No surprise charges. Perfect.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct. The only time you might see charges is for international calls made over Wi-Fi, which are billed at our standard international long-distance rates. But for calls to any number in the US, you are all set.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Got it. That's very clear. Thank you for clarifying that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. My goal is to make sure you have all the information you need. I'll add a note about this clarification to your file as well.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You're very thorough.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I believe in resolving an issue completely so you don't have to call us back. It saves you time in the long run.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I can't argue with that. Okay, for real this time, that's all I have. Thank you again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure, Mr. Williams. Have a great day and enjoy your crystal-clear calls from the basement!

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Haha, I will. Bye now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.
